issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff in a partition suit cannot withdraw the suit to defeat another shareholder’s purchase option after requesting a sale and the other shareholder has offered to buy the plaintiff’s share at a valuation.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought sale of jointly owned property on the ground that it could not reasonably or conveniently be divided.
The defendant stated in the written statement that, if the property was found incapable of division, the defendant was willing to buy the plaintiff’s share at a court-determined valuation.
A commissioner had difficulty suggesting a division, and the trial judge had formed a prima facie view that division by metes and bounds was not possible.
Before a final decision or valuation, the plaintiff sought to withdraw the suit with liberty to bring a fresh suit.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff could not withdraw the suit so as to deprive the defendant of the advantage of buying the plaintiff’s share at a valuation; the suit had to be restored for consideration of the defendant’s request.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2 and 3 of the Partition Act, when a shareholder requests sale in a partition suit and another shareholder applies for leave to buy the requesting shareholder’s share at a valuation, the court must order a valuation and offer the share to that shareholder. The resulting advantage is a privilege that the plaintiff cannot defeat by withdrawing the suit under Order 23 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. A defendant seeking a share in a partition suit is in the position of a plaintiff, and one plaintiff cannot withdraw so as to defeat another’s claim. The Court applied Tukaram Mahadu Tandel v. Ramchandra Mahadu Tandel and distinguished the circumstances addressed in Bijayananda Patnaik v. Satrughna Sahu and Hulas Rai Baij Nath v. Firm K. B. Dass & Co.

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit between co-owners seeking partition of jointly owned property.
predicates.plaintiff_requested_sale: The plaintiff asked the court to sell the property rather than divide it.
predicates.co_shareholder_offered_to_buy_at_valuati: Another shareholder notified the court that they were willing to buy the plaintiff’s share at a court-determined valuation.
predicates.plaintiff_sought_withdrawal: The plaintiff asked to withdraw the suit after the other shareholder had offered to buy at a valuation.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff in a partition suit requests a sale, another shareholder offers to buy the plaintiff’s share at a valuation, and the plaintiff then seeks withdrawal, withdrawal is denied to preserve the purchase option.

issues.legal_issue: A conclusive finding that property cannot be divided is not required before a shareholder’s purchase request may be considered; it is sufficient that the court finds division prima facie not reasonably or conveniently possible.
material_facts: The plaintiff requested sale of the jointly owned property, asserting that it could not be divided by metes and bounds.
The trial judge had formed a prima facie view that division was not possible, but had not made a final finding on divisibility.
The defendant had offered to buy the plaintiff’s share at a valuation if the court found the property incapable of division.
issues.conclusion: The trial judge’s prima facie view was sufficient for the proceedings; a positive final finding of incapability of division was not required at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2 and 3 of the Partition Act require that it appear to the court that a division cannot reasonably or conveniently be made; they do not require a conclusive positive finding of incapability before the other shareholder’s purchase request can be considered.

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit between co-owners seeking partition of jointly owned property.
predicates.plaintiff_requested_sale: The plaintiff asked the court to sell the property rather than divide it.
predicates.court_found_division_prima_facie_unworka: The court formed a preliminary view that the property could not reasonably or conveniently be divided.
predicates.co_shareholder_offered_to_buy_at_valuati: Another shareholder notified the court that they were willing to buy the plaintiff’s share at a court-determined valuation.

issues.definition: A preliminary judicial view that division is unworkable is sufficient to consider a co-shareholder’s purchase request when the plaintiff has requested sale in a partition suit and the co-shareholder has offered to buy at a valuation.

issues.legal_issue: A co-shareholder can invoke the purchase procedure by notifying the court in a pleading that they are willing to buy at a valuation, without filing a separate formal application.
material_facts: The defendant denied that the property was incapable of division but stated in the written statement that, if the court found it incapable of division, the defendant was willing to buy the plaintiff’s share at a valuation set by the court.
The plaintiff had requested that the property be sold.
issues.conclusion: The defendant’s conditional statement in the written statement was sufficient compliance with the requirement to apply for leave to buy at a valuation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) of the Partition Act does not require a formal application in every case; the other shareholder need only inform or notify the court of willingness to buy the share at a valuation.
